text: Hugh has obsessive‑compulsive disorder (OCD). Hugh’s childhood was difficult. His mother had
an obsession with germs, insisting on excessive cleanliness.
Suggest two different explanations of why Hugh has OCD. [4]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline what is meant by ‘cultural differences’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain one reason why cultural differences could affect the diagnosis of an anxiety disorder.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how Habiba’s therapist can use systematic desensitisation to treat Habiba’s phobia.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain one weakness of systematic desensitisation.

text: Habiba has a phobia of flying insects. She is afraid of the noise they make and is very scared if one
lands on her. Habiba’s therapist recommends that she is treated using systematic desensitisation.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists investigating the treatment and management of mood (affective)
disorders have discovered about:
• MAOI anti‑depressants, and
• Ellis’s rational emotive behaviour therapy (REBT).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists investigating the treatment and management of mood (affective)
disorders have discovered about:
• MAOI anti‑depressants, and
• Ellis’s rational emotive behaviour therapy (REBT),
including a discussion of reductionism versus holism.
Evaluation in your answer can include strengths, weaknesses and a discussion of issues and
debates. 
Section B: Consumer Psychology

text: Abdul wants to purchase a chair from a website. The website is designed so that comparisons
between items are not easy to make.
Suggest two decision‑making strategies Abdul is likely to use when purchasing his chair. [4]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline what is meant by ‘determinism’, including an example from choice heuristics.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain one strength of using the determinism side of the determinism versus free‑will debate
to understand choice heuristics.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Identify which type of shopper spatial behaviour pattern would be most appropriate to
describe:
• Zelda
• Louis.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Frank is a different type of shopper from Zelda and Louis. He shows a different spatial
behaviour pattern.
Suggest how Frank could behave in the supermarket.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain one problem that psychologists may have when investigating shoppers’ spatial
behaviour patterns.

text: Supermarket shoppers do not all behave in the same way. Shoppers can be categorised into
five types based on their different spatial behaviour patterns. Zelda visits all of the aisles of the
supermarket when she does her main shopping. However, Louis spends a short time in the
supermarket and visits only a few aisles.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about types of advertising and advertising
techniques:
• the Yale model of communication, and
• a study about types of advertising media.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about types of advertising and advertising
techniques:
• the Yale model of communication, and
• a study about types of advertising media,
including a discussion of objective and subjective data.
Evaluation in your answer can include strengths, weaknesses and a discussion of issues and
debates. 
Section C: Health Psychology

text: A university student, Chloe, thinks that she has less chance of becoming ill than other students.
She also thinks that she has more chance of living longer than other students. This suggests
unrealistic optimism in Chloe’s health beliefs.
Suggest two reasons why Chloe may have unrealistic optimism in her health beliefs. [4]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline what is meant by the debate between individual and situational explanations.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why one strategy for improving health has a situational explanation.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest two different measures of pain that Omar’s practitioner could use with him.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
For one of the measures of pain you suggested in part (a):
Explain one weakness of this measure of pain.

text: Omar is in hospital with chest pain. His practitioner wants to investigate this by assessing Omar’s
pain.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists investigating practitioner diagnosis have discovered about:
• making a diagnosis (disclosure of information, false positive and false negative
diagnosis), and
• presenting a diagnosis.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists investigating practitioner diagnosis have discovered about:
• making a diagnosis (disclosure of information, false positive and false negative
diagnosis), and
• presenting a diagnosis,
including a discussion of validity.
Evaluation in your answer can include strengths, weaknesses and a discussion of issues and
debates. 
Section D: Organisational Psychology

text: Celeste is a member of a newly formed school council. This is a group of student representatives
who make decisions, such as what should be on the school menu and whether to have recycling
bins or a new drinks machine.
Suggest the stages of group development that the school council could go through as they make
decisions. [4]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by a ‘nomothetic approach’, including an example from a need theory
of motivation at work.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain how a need theory of motivation at work could be investigated using an idiographic
approach.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Suggest two ways Tatpara could use extrinsic motivators with the carpet factory workers to
increase production.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
For one of your suggestions in part (a):
Explain one strength of this suggestion, other than to increase production.

text: Tatpara is the manager at a carpet factory. He is concerned about low production at his factory.
Tatpara believes this may be due to a lack of motivation in the workers.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about temporal conditions of work
environments:
• rapid rotation and slow rotation shiftwork, and
• a study about the effects of shiftwork on health and accidents.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about temporal conditions of work environments:
• rapid rotation and slow rotation shiftwork, and
• a study about the effects of shiftwork on health and accidents,
including a discussion of quantitative and qualitative data.
Evaluation in your answer can include strengths, weaknesses and a discussion of issues and
debates.
